chapter: Cabarets and the Red Light District
title: Girls' dress, the cribs and the Hans Nagel cabaret
summary: Describes the dancers' dress, the cribs in the red light district, and names the cabaret as Huntz and Nagel's, with its owners.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What do they wear? They wear like nice gay them dresses, clean. It's regular dresses. Yeah. See women's land made their money on their legs, big legs. And you see the legs up to the air back in those days, man. Rain, I used to pay a dime to go downtown, a nickel. I used to see women get on the street called Ray's dress up so I could look at the legs. Because you didn't see no look at the wood of dresses starting. Oh I see, yeah. That thing going? Yeah. Yeah. That's good. And now the cribs, you see that was in the red light district. See, now the girl, now if you want to go out with the girl, see, 50 cents a dollar, whatever you want to give her, you know. And when she finishes with you, she come on back, get ready to go to the dance and give her. Oh you mean the girls have their cribs, but they will come to the dance? They'll come to the dance, but they'll all have a place where they go. See, they all had a place to go. They're sporting girls, you know. Yes, I understand. Sometimes it'd be right upstairs. The boss would have a place where they go, take you upstairs in the room, you see. Or you pay for the room. What was the name of this cabaret where you were? Hans Nagel. What? Hans Nagel and Eddie Groce, that's what they named it. Oh, I see. See, Hans Nagel, he was a Jew, but I don't know what Eddie Groce, I don't know what he was, but he was very quiet. He was a nice man.
What kind of a band did they have there? We had a seven-piece band.
A seven-piece band. King all over. Uh-huh. That was in 19…
